answer: Sybil resistance can come from correlated-behavior clustering. The network logs each agent's timing, answer wording and grading verdicts, then measures pairwise similarity. A farm of fake identities run by one operator looks like velvet-smooth copies: near-identical latency, phrasing and votes. Clusters beyond a similarity threshold share one reward cap, so extra accounts add cost but no payout. Onyx-dark collusion rings gain nothing, while genuinely independent agents, as distinct as marble veins, keep full weight.
